newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia allows foreign palm oil investments.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia allows foreign palm oil investments.

text.p: Foreign investors are to be allowed to set up oil palm plantations in eastern Indonesia if they involve smallholders, a local business newspaper reported on Tuesday, quoting Agriculture Minister Syarifuddin Baharsyah.
Bisnis Indonesia quoted him as saying a lot of land was available in the eastern region, which is generally shunned by foreign investors because of the lack of infrastucture to support industries.
Baharsyah said foreign investors had mainly showed interest in the more developed western part of the archipelago.
"Because of this, we want to channel investments in plantations into eastern Indonesia, including foreign investments in the oil palm sector," he was quoted as saying.
The government earlier this month announced a temporary ban on foreign investments in the oil palm industry pending a study on foreign presence in the sector.
The Jakarta Post newspaper on Tuesday quoted Baharsyah as saying the ban only covered western Indonesia, which takes in Kalimantan and Sumatra where the main palm oil estates are found.
